newsitem.title: JAPAN: Prosecutors likely to indict DKB--reports.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors likely to indict DKB--reports.

text.p: Prosecutors are likely to indict Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) for alleged violations of the banking law by concealing information regarding a scandal involving corporate racketeers, two leading Japanese newspapers said on Thursday.
DKB could be indicted as early as next week if the Finance Ministry files a criminal complaint with prosecutors against the bank, the Mainichi Shimbun said.
The Asahi Shimbun said even though the bank would face a fine of less than 500,000 yen, it would be very unusual for a violation of the banking law to be taken up as a criminal matter.
Prosecutors are also likely to indict DKB's former chairman Tadashi Okuda on Friday on suspicion of illegally making bank loans to a racketeer, the Mainichi said.
Prosecutors were not immediately available for comment on the reports.
